name: Waldorf Astoria Berlin
positioning: Waldorf Astoria hotel in a City West skyscraper by the Kurfürstendamm, with Art Deco-style bars and a fifth-floor spa
best_for: Travelers who want a City West base by the Kurfürstendamm, across the street from the Zoo and Tiergarten park
Families wanting a two-room Family Deluxe Room

facts.text: The hotel is in Berlin City West, by the Kurfürstendamm shopping district.
The Berlin Zoo and Tiergarten park are just across the street from the hotel.
The hotel is set in a skyscraper in City West.
It is the sole Waldorf Astoria in Germany.
ROCA blends Italian cuisine with the urban spirit of New York.
ROCA has a hand-painted ceiling mural.
The Lang Bar has Art Deco surroundings and serves Film Noir-inspired drinks.
The Library Lounge on the 15th floor serves afternoon tea with views across the city.
The Waldorf Astoria Spa is on the fifth floor.
All rooms and suites feature a marble bathroom, Nespresso coffee machine, dining table and safe.
Tower Suites on the upper floors have a kitchenette and access to the tower lift.
The Family Deluxe Room combines a King Deluxe and an adjoining Twin Deluxe Room and sleeps two adults and two children.

highlights.text: Peacock Alley is named after a corridor that connected the original Waldorf Hotel to the Astoria in New York.
Rooms have a dining table for private dining, a nod to Waldorf Astoria, where room service is said to have been invented.
The spa has a cloud-shaped pool, Finnish sauna, steam room, five therapy rooms and a terrace.
The Lang Bar channels the film director Fritz Lang.
The Champagne and Eggs all-day breakfast serves Waldorf Astoria inventions such as Eggs Benedict.

considerations.text: Spa access costs hotel guests 15 euros per person per day; it is complimentary for Tower Suite guests and Hilton Honors Silver, Gold and Diamond members.
Children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult in the spa.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the high-end positioning.
